  • The rate of change is [MATH: 10,] since Fred bakes a batch of [MATH: 10] additional cookies each day.

Substituting into the formula, we reach

[MATH: C|= A + 10n.]

[MATH: C|= A + 10n; (35)|= A + 10(3); 35|= A + 30; 5|= A]

So, the formula is

[MATH: C|= 5 + 10n.]

sections.readable_text:
A bus leaves town for a [MATH: 270] mile journey. The remaining distance, [MATH: D], to complete the trip after [MATH: n] hours is given by
[MATH: D = 270 - 45 n.]
How long does it take for the bus to travel one-half of the total distance?

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
One half of the total distance is [MATH: \dfrac{270}{2} = 135.]

If the bus has traveled half the distance, the remaining distance is also equal to half the distance. So, we want to solve for the number of hours [MATH: n] it takes until the bus has [MATH: D=135] miles remaining.

We can do this by substituting into the equation [MATH: D=270-45n] and solving for [MATH: n] as follows:

[MATH: 135|= 270 − 45n; 135 + 45n|= 270; 45n|= 270 − 135; 45n|= 135; n|= (135)/(45); n|= 3.]

Therefore, the bus takes [MATH: 3] hours to travel half of the total distance.
